explain.ind.working_days.what: The number of days in the range that had at least one commit.
explain.ind.working_days.how: The core (`indicators.rs`) counts the rows in the daily statistics (`DayStats`) that `day_stats` groups by commit date — a day without a single commit simply does not exist in that list, so it is not counted.
explain.ind.working_days.read: A measure (it counts what is recorded in git, not an estimate). A higher number usually means a steadier rhythm; a low number over a long range is a sign of a pause, not necessarily less work (work without a commit stays invisible).
explain.ind.commits.what: The total number of commits on the tracked branch from `since` to the end of the range.
explain.ind.commits.how: The core (`indicators.rs`) counts the length of `input.commits` — the list of commits the core (`parse_git_log`, `gitlog.rs`) structures from the `git log` text; `io` only reads that text from disk, it does not recognize commits.
explain.ind.commits.read: A measure. A raw count without any judgement of a commit's size or importance — ten small fixes and one large refactor count the same.
explain.ind.commits_per_day.what: The average number of commits per working day (a day with at least one commit).
explain.ind.commits_per_day.how: The core divides commits by working days (`indicators.rs`, rounded to one decimal) — if the range has no working day at all, the division is skipped and the value stays 0.
explain.ind.commits_per_day.read: A measure derived from two other measures. It tracks rhythm, not quality — many small commits raise the number without any relation to how much work was actually done.
explain.ind.deliveries.what: The number of entries in the diary (the project's diary, per the profile's convention) written since `since`.
explain.ind.deliveries.how: The core counts the length of the delivery list that the core (`parse_diary`, `diary.rs`) extracts from the diary text by the pattern in the profile, before it reaches this calculation (`indicators.rs`); `io` only reads that text from disk.
explain.ind.deliveries.read: A measure, but dependent on diary discipline: a project that works but does not record deliveries drops out silently here, even though commits exist.
explain.ind.deliveries_per_day.what: The average number of deliveries per working day.
explain.ind.deliveries_per_day.how: The core divides deliveries by working days (`indicators.rs`, rounded to one decimal), the same pattern as the commits-per-day indicator.
explain.ind.deliveries_per_day.read: A measure. A low number does not necessarily mean little was delivered — it can mean deliveries were not written into the diary in the form the profile recognizes.
explain.ind.hours.what: An estimate of hours worked from the gaps between consecutive commits — the same proxy the old `RAD.xlsx` used, but corrected (S-007).
explain.ind.hours.how: `hours.rs` (`hours_per_day`) sorts commits by author time, then for each commit looks at the gap to the previous one: a gap shorter than the pause threshold (`session_gap_hours` from the profile) counts as work; a larger gap, or the first commit of a session, adds a fixed session start (`session_start_hours` from the profile).
explain.ind.hours.read: A proxy, not a measurement of actually spent time — nobody used a stopwatch. Sorting by author time prevents negative hours from a cherry-pick (a known flaw of the original `RAD.xlsx`), but the estimate stays rough: long thinking without a commit stays invisible, and dense committing inflates the number.
explain.ind.commits_per_hour.what: How many commits landed per one estimated hour of work.
explain.ind.commits_per_hour.how: The core divides commits by hours (`indicators.rs`) — the divisor is the same proxy from `hours.rs`, so this number inherits all of its shortcomings.
explain.ind.commits_per_hour.read: A proxy derived from a proxy. Useful for comparing the same project over time, not for an absolute judgement of productivity — it rests on an hour estimate, not a measured duration.
explain.ind.lines_changed.what: The total number of changed lines (added plus deleted) across every commit in the range.
explain.ind.lines_changed.how: The core (`indicators.rs`) walks the files of every commit and sums the added and deleted lines (`FileChange`, from `git log --numstat`).
explain.ind.lines_changed.read: A measure. A large number does not necessarily mean large progress — a generated file or a mass rename raises the number without proportional value.
explain.ind.test_lines.what: The number of changed lines on paths the profile recognizes as tests.
explain.ind.test_lines.how: The core sums the test lines from every day (`DayStats`) — `day_stats` (`days.rs`) itself checks whether a changed file's path is a test path (`Profile::is_test_path`) while it walks the commits; `io` is not involved in that decision.
explain.ind.test_lines.read: A measure, dependent on the profile: a project whose test paths the profile does not recognize will show 0 even with real tests. Check `.sokratis/profile.json` if the number is unexpectedly low.
explain.ind.test_share.what: The share of changed lines that went into tests and gates, relative to all changed lines.
explain.ind.test_share.how: The core divides test lines by changed lines (`indicators.rs`, rounded to three decimals; when there are no changed lines, the division is skipped and the value stays 0).
explain.ind.test_share.read: A measure. A higher share usually means more disciplined testing, but it also depends on whether the profile recognizes all of the project's test paths (see the test-lines indicator).
explain.ind.deploys.what: The number of diary entries marked as a deploy to production.
explain.ind.deploys.how: The core counts deliveries marked as a deploy (`indicators.rs`) — that flag is set by `parse_diary` (`diary.rs`) while parsing the diary: a 🚀 marker in the title OR the `diary_deploy` pattern from the profile.
explain.ind.deploys.read: A measure, dependent on diary marking discipline — a deploy not recorded with that pattern is not counted.
explain.ind.debugging_commits.what: The number of commits classified as debugging (a bug fix).
explain.ind.debugging_commits.how: The core counts commits for which the classifier (`kinds.rs`, `effective_kind`) returns the debugging kind — the kind comes from a manual override if one exists, otherwise from the classifier reading the commit's subject.
explain.ind.debugging_commits.read: A measure, but dependent on the classifier: a commit subject that does not follow the convention (e.g. "fix:") may stay misclassified until someone corrects it by hand (an override in the Diary).
explain.ind.debugging_share.what: The share of debugging commits among all commits in the range.
explain.ind.debugging_share.how: The core divides debugging commits by all commits (`indicators.rs`, rounded to three decimals).
explain.ind.debugging_share.read: A measure. A high share over the long run is a sign of instability; an occasional spike is not alarming on its own — check the commit kinds in the Diary before drawing a conclusion.
explain.ind.docs_share.what: The share of commits classified as documentation upkeep among all commits.
explain.ind.docs_share.how: The core divides the number of commits with the documentation kind (`kinds.rs`, `effective_kind`) by the total number of commits (`indicators.rs`, rounded to three decimals).
explain.ind.docs_share.read: A measure. A low share does not necessarily mean neglected documentation — also check the score in the Documentation view, which looks at content, not just the commit count.
explain.ind.ci_fixes.what: The number of commits whose subject reports fixing a failing CI (continuous integration) run.
explain.ind.ci_fixes.how: The core counts commits whose lowercased subject matches the CI-fix pattern from the profile (`indicators.rs`).
explain.ind.ci_fixes.read: A measure, dependent on the profile and on commit-subject discipline — a fix that does not mention the pattern (e.g. "ci:") is not counted, even though CI actually failed.
explain.ind.owner_driven_deliveries.what: The number of diary deliveries whose title mentions the project owner as the trigger.
explain.ind.owner_driven_deliveries.how: The core counts deliveries whose lowercased title contains the owner's name from the profile (`indicators.rs`).
explain.ind.owner_driven_deliveries.read: A measure, dependent on diary title discipline — it shows how many deliveries the owner's finding triggered, not how much the owner contributed overall.
explain.ind.closed_phases_in_range.what: The number of the project's closed phases whose end date is on or after the start of the observed range (the end of the range is not checked).
explain.ind.closed_phases_in_range.how: The core counts closed phases whose end date is `>= since` (`indicators.rs`) — the upper bound of the range (`until`) is not checked; before that, `phases.rs` already drops a closed phase with no matching commit in the repository, so someone else's history (from the default profile) does not enter the count.
explain.ind.closed_phases_in_range.read: A measure. A low number in a short range is expected — phases take days to weeks, not one per day.
explain.ind.closed_phase_avg_days.what: The average duration (in days) of the closed phases the project has in its profile.
explain.ind.closed_phase_avg_days.how: The core computes the mean duration across every closed phase (`indicators.rs`, rounded to one decimal); each phase's duration is its start/end date difference plus one day (`phases.rs`, `days_between`).
explain.ind.closed_phase_avg_days.read: A measure, but computed over ALL closed phases from the profile, not only those in the closed-phases-in-range indicator — the two numbers look at different sets of phases, so one should not be divided by the other.
explain.overview.signals.what: The number of signals by severity (info/warn/alert) for this project, from the last computed report.
explain.overview.signals.how: The interface reads `SignalCounts` from `ProjectSummary` (`apps/desktop/src-tauri/src/summary.rs`) — rules (`rules/`, e.g. unmerged branches, docs lag) evaluate the report, and `snapshot.rs::worst_severity` picks the worst color for the row.
explain.overview.signals.read: A summary, not a list — open the project to see individual signals with evidence in the signal bar. No signals does not mean the project is flawless, only that none of the built-in rules noticed anything.
explain.overview.last_commit.what: The time and subject of the latest commit in the project's last computed report.
explain.overview.last_commit.how: `apps/desktop/src-tauri/src/summary.rs` (`summarize`) looks for the commit with the highest `author_time` in `Report.commits` — not the last one in the list, since list order is not guaranteed.
explain.overview.last_commit.read: Shows when the project last got a commit, not when Sokratis was last opened. An empty field means the report for this project has not been computed yet.
explain.overview.worktrees.what: The number of worktrees git sees for this project.
explain.overview.worktrees.how: `io` (`git.rs`, `worktrees`) reads `git worktree list --porcelain`; a project is defined through `git-common-dir` (S-015), so every worktree of the same repository counts as ONE project.
explain.overview.worktrees.read: More than one worktree is normal when working on several branches in parallel — the number says nothing about progress, only how many copies of the repository are open.
explain.tempo.bars.what: Commit or hour bars per day in the selected range, depending on the switch above the chart.
explain.tempo.bars.how: The chart draws `DayStats.commits` or `DayStats.hours` from `metrics/days.rs`/`metrics/hours.rs`, with no extra calculation in the interface (S-012) — it only picks which column to show.
explain.tempo.bars.read: A day with no commit has no bar at all, not a zero-height bar — compare with the table below for the exact list of days.
explain.tempo.cumulative.what: The running total of commits across the range, one row per day.
explain.tempo.cumulative.how: The line draws `DayStats.commits_cumulative` (`metrics/days.rs`) directly — the core already sums it while assembling the days, the interface does not recompute it.
explain.tempo.cumulative.read: A line that only ever rises (never falls) because it is the sum of commits since the range started — the slope tells you about pace, not the height alone.
explain.tempo.hours.what: The estimated hours worked per day (the same proxy as the hours indicator).
explain.tempo.hours.how: The table column reads `DayStats.hours`, which `metrics/hours.rs` (`hours_per_day`) computes from the gaps between commits sorted by `author_time` (S-007: sorting prevents negative hours from a cherry-pick); the pause threshold (`session_gap_hours`) and session start (`session_start_hours`) come from the profile.
explain.tempo.hours.read: A proxy, not measured time — the same caveat as the "hours worked" indicator in Indicators.
explain.kinds.ring.what: A ring showing the share of commits by work kind (planning, documentation, execution, polish, debugging) in the selected range.
explain.kinds.ring.how: Each ring segment is a ready-made percentage computed by `metrics/kinds.rs` (`kind_stats`) — the kind comes from `classify.rs`, and a manual override from the Diary always outranks the classifier (`effective_kind`).
explain.kinds.ring.read: A share of commits by kind, not by time or lines — one large polish commit counts the same as one tiny one.
explain.kinds.share.what: The share of commits of this kind among all commits in the range.
explain.kinds.share.how: `KindStats.share` (`metrics/kinds.rs`) divides the commit count of the kind by the total commit count, rounded to three decimals — the interface only prints it as a percentage (S-012).
explain.kinds.share.read: Depends on the classifier and Diary overrides (the same caveat as the ring) — a commit whose subject does not follow the convention can land in the wrong kind until someone corrects it by hand.
explain.phases.days.what: How long the phase lasted, in days.
explain.phases.days.how: Closed phases: `metrics/phases.rs` (`closed_phases`) computes `days_between(from, to) + 1` from the dates in the profile. Running phases: `active_phases` computes the same from the date of the first tagged commit to today.
explain.phases.days.read: Calendar days, not working days — a weekend or a pause with no commit counts the same as a day of active work.
explain.phases.commits.what: The number of commits carrying this phase's tag (e.g. "F2/3") in their subject.
explain.phases.commits.how: Two different mechanisms depending on the phase's state (`metrics/phases.rs`): closed phases (`closed_phases`) count commits whose subject matches that phase's OWN pattern (`ClosedPhase.tag_pattern` from the profile, `profile.rs`) — no parent/child hierarchy. Running phases (`active_phases`) instead read the SHARED `phase_tag` pattern from the profile through `classify::phase_tag` and count a commit if the extracted tag matches the phase id or starts with "{id}/" ("F2/3" belongs to "F2").
explain.phases.commits.read: A commit without a phase tag in its subject is not counted toward any phase — a low number can also mean subjects do not follow the convention, not necessarily that the phase is small.
explain.phases.bricks_per_day.what: The average number of bricks (finished plan items) per day the phase lasted.
explain.phases.bricks_per_day.how: The interface (`views/helpers.ts`, `bricksPerDay`) divides `done_bricks` by `days` — the only calculation in this view the core does not yet hand over ready-made (a recorded debt owed to `core`).
explain.phases.bricks_per_day.read: A number derived from two others, not a core measurement — when the duration is unknown, it shows blank instead of dividing by zero.
explain.diary.kind.what: The work kind for this commit (planning, documentation, execution, polish, debugging) and its subkind (brick, gate/measure, deploy, other); a "manual" mark next to the row means the kind was set by hand (an override), not by the classifier.
explain.diary.kind.how: The kind comes from `classify::classify_kind` over the commit's subject, unless `overrides.json` has a manual entry for that SHA (`kinds.rs`, `effective_kind`) — an override always wins. The dropdown in the row changes the override live through `api.setOverride`, and the core recomputes the report right away.
explain.diary.kind.read: Classification is a heuristic over the commit subject, not an understanding of the content — when it looks wrong, fix it here instead of letting the distrust linger in numbers elsewhere in the report.
explain.deliveries.list.what: Deliveries read from the project's diary (dated headings, per the profile's convention) in the selected range.
explain.deliveries.list.how: The core (`parse_diary`, `diary.rs`) extracts deliveries from the diary text using the pattern from the profile into a list of `Delivery` — `io` only reads that text from disk, it does not recognize deliveries. The kind and deploy flag are determined the same way as for a commit (`classify_kind`, the deploy pattern).
explain.deliveries.list.read: The list depends on diary discipline: work that happened but was not written up by the convention does not show up here, even though the commit exists.
explain.visions.totals.what: The number of visions by state (e.g. how many are "idea", how many "running").
explain.visions.totals.how: `metrics/visions.rs` (`vision_totals`) counts visions by the `state` field and sorts states alphabetically — state is free text the user types into the form, the core neither translates it nor restricts it to a fixed list.
explain.visions.totals.read: The totals track however many distinct states the user has ever typed — a spelling difference (e.g. "running" vs. "Running") counts as two different states.
explain.visions.percent.what: The completion percentage of a vision, if one was entered.
explain.visions.percent.how: A manual field from `.sokratis/visions.json` (`Vision.percent`, 0–100) — the core does not compute it from commits or phases, the interface only prints it as a percentage.
explain.visions.percent.read: A user's own estimate, not a measurement of progress from git — a blank field (no percentage) differs from "0%": one means unknown, the other means not started yet.
explain.docs.score.what: The documentation cleanliness score, from 0 to 100.
explain.docs.score.how: `docs.rs` (`docs_health`) subtracts a penalty from 100 for every finding (dead link, file missing from the index, multiple active plans, no active plan, diary content in a definition doc, lag, key-file over budget — seven kinds) — each finding's weight comes from `docs_weights` in the profile.
explain.docs.score.read: The score measures how well documentation is ORGANIZED (links, index, one active plan), not how thorough or well-written it is — 100 does not mean the documentation is complete, only that none of these checks failed.
explain.docs.lag.what: How many days the diary and changelog are behind the last code commit.
explain.docs.lag.how: `docs.rs` (`lag`, `lag_days`) subtracts the diary/changelog's last-change time from the last code commit's time and divides by 86,400 (seconds in a day); when the difference is zero or negative, it returns 0. The row shows as soon as both times are known — for EVERY value, not only ones above the threshold; the profile's threshold (`docs_lag_warn_days`) only decides whether the lag becomes a finding (and thus affects the score), not whether the row is shown.
explain.docs.lag.read: Days since CODE pulled ahead of DOCUMENTATION, not the other way around — the number shows even when it is zero (documentation is current); the row only disappears when the dates are unknown (e.g. the diary was never changed), not because the lag is small.
explain.docs.findings.what: The list of concrete problems the documentation check found (dead links, files missing from the index, multiple active plans, and similar).
explain.docs.findings.how: `docs.rs` (`docs_health`) fills the `Finding` list from six independent checks (dead links, indexing, active plans, chronology in a definition doc, lag, key-file budget) — each finding carries a path and, when known, a line.
explain.docs.findings.read: Each finding is a reason the score is not 100 — the button next to it copies the full file path to make it easier to open and fix.
explain.signals.severity.what: The severity of a signal for this project: info, warn, or alert.
explain.signals.severity.how: Rules from `rules/` (e.g. unmerged branches, docs lag) each return a `Severity` (`model.rs`: info < warn < alert, in that order); `snapshot.rs::alerts_raised` tracks ONLY the transition into alert between two computations, so the system notification does not fire on every report (S-020).
explain.signals.severity.read: An alert needs attention now; a warning is worth checking but not urgent; info is just an observation. The evidence behind the title (click "evidence") shows EXACTLY what the rule saw.
